entertainment.title: Paramount’s “About Us” Was Filled With Fake Latin for Months — and Nobody Noticed
entertainment.summary: “Lorem Ipsum Dolor,” reads the dummy text prematurely posted on one of the studio’s corporate websites. Couldn’t have put it better ourselves.
entertainment.body:
Logo text There are many ways to learn about a company. Read its annual report. Follow its earnings calls. Or, in Paramount ‘s case, click on its “About Paramount” page, where, until very recently, you’d find several paragraphs of incomprehensible gibberish alongside a photograph of a fictional mob boss.

“Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet,” it read , “consectetur adipiscing elit.”

The page, which had apparently been live for months, was obviously a work in progress — Latin dummy text is what web designers use as a placeholder until supplied with real words. But it was still a head-scratcher, considering Paramount’s new overlords at Skydance have had more than a year since the merger to whip up fresh corporate boilerplate.

The image of Marlon Brando as Don Corleone kind of made sense — The Godfather remains one of the studio’s historic high points. Still, one can’t help but wonder if perhaps Top Gun might have been a safer choice. Or SpongeBob . Because with David Ellison now running Paramount and his billionaire father, Larry, backing the enterprise, it’s probably best to avoid associations with any other sort of family business.

There were other parts lower down on the page that also needed attention (the same three executives were listed as running multiple divisions, and two of them don’t even work there anymore). But, of course, these sorts of technical snafus happen. Remember when Netflix mixed up its blurb for a Tinker Bell movie with the synopsis for Tangerine ? (“Her pimp cheated on her while she was locked up. Now this working girl sets out to claim her pound of flesh.”)

Paramount, which didn’t respond to Rambling’s request for comment, finally did get around to fixing it; last week, the unfinished “About Paramount” page was replaced by an “About Skydance” page with actual corporate copy. This time, there was no picture of Brando.

entertainment.title: Cheesecake Factory’s Biggest Fans Are Actually Democrats
entertainment.summary: Even before Obama’s crack about Trump’s White House gilt trip, the Cheesecake Factory was having a moment on TV and online.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Thanks to Barack Obama , the Cheesecake Factory is now famous for something other than its ginormous portions. Indeed, the former president’s quip dissing Donald Trump’s decorating choices — “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened up a Cheesecake Factory” — put the family-friendly chain in the red-hot center of multiple news cycles, with the Trump administration responding to the “elitist attack” by dispatching Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to actually eat at the place and then, on election night, having Cheesecake Factory food delivered to the White House. As if the election results weren’t hard enough for Republicans to swallow. Related Stories Lifestyle Kel Mitchell Bringing 'Kel's Burger Fest' to Los Angeles: "It's a Full-On Burger Bonanza" TV Meet the British Foodie Demystifying the Michelin Guide's Secrets

What caught Rambling’s attention, though, was how Cheesecake Factory had been popping up on the cultural radar even before it started making headlines over Trump’s gilt complex. Two days before Obama’s joke, Netflix dropped season three of Nobody Wants This , which included a scene in which Joanne is considering Noah’s parents’ house as a venue for their wedding. “Candelabra, candelabra, candelabra,” her friend Sebastien intones while they examine pictures of the home. “Looks like a Cheesecake Factory. You can’t get married here.”

In September, Cheesecake Factory had a moment on TikTok, as well, after a Minneapolis nail technician posted a video recommending the restaurant’s Cajun salmon, tweaked with her own fussy modifications (adding shrimp, swapping in loaded potatoes, extra sauce). The video went viral, catching the attention of tennis ace Coco Gauff and online food reviewer Keith Lee (“This is a nine out of 10”), ultimately pulling more than 5 million views.

All this attention — even Obama’s joke — clearly hasn’t hurt Cheesecake Factory’s bottom line. The company recently reported third-quarter revenue of $1.03 billion, up 14 percent from the same period last year. Ironically, despite all the acid reflux-like outrage from the White House over Obama’s crack, the majority of Cheesecake Factory’s customers appear to have voted for Democrats in the midterms, at least according to conservative political scientist Richard Hanania. He crunched the numbers and found that voters who lived in counties that included a Cheesecake Factory tended to favor Democrats by an average of nearly 30 points.

entertainment.title: Aspyn Ovard Reveals 10-Year Secret Behind Parker Ferris Breakup
entertainment.summary: Aspyn Ovard is sharing her truth about the end of her marriage to Parker Ferris. Two years after their divorce, the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County star revealed the infamous “10-year...
entertainment.body:
Aspyn Ovard is sharing her truth about the end of her marriage to Parker Ferris .

Two years after their divorce, the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County star revealed the infamous “10-year secret” fans have long awaited to learn: the real reason behind her breakup from Ferris.

“Publicly, I'd never shared why we got divorced,” Ovard said on the Nov. 12 premiere of the first season of the Hulu series. “When Parker and I were getting married, we were definitely—I thought, actually—we were on the same page about where we stood with drinking and smoking and things like that.”

While the YouTuber—who shares daughters Cove , 7, Lola , 5, and Elle , 2, with her ex—assumed she and Ferris both abstained from alcohol, she learned her then-husband wasn’t being truthful.

“My dad struggled with alcoholism, so the only version of him that I knew was some level of intoxicated,” Ovard recalled. “Whenever he would come home, and just the sound of his work boots, just like a dark cloud, over the house.”

“Finding out that Parker had been drinking behind my back for years, it was literally earth-shattering,” she continued, nodding in agreement when a producer asked if that was the big secret. “He went through so much to hide it from me, and the fact that my husband, who was supposed to be the safest person, would do that to me.”

The 30-year-old became emotional as she shared how learning of Ferris' hidden behavior impacted her, while also revealing how the timing made the situation even more difficult.

As Ovard told the cameras, “For him to know what alcoholism did to my family, to find all of this out two months after my dad died from alcoholism hurt so bad.”

entertainment.title: LNGSHOT Talk Musical Attitude & Group’s Turning Point: ‘S.W.I.S.H.’
entertainment.summary: Ahead of the EP's release, Billboard Korea sat down with LNGSHOT for an exclusive interview.
entertainment.body:
LNGSHOT return with their new EP S.W.I.S.H. The release continues the “hustle” the group has kept up since debuting in January this year with their first EP SHOT CALLERS . Since then, they have put out two mixtapes, the EP Training Day collecting their pre-debut work, and a string of OSTs and singles.

S.W.I.S.H. captures LNGSHOT’s style in a different way from SHOT CALLERS . Every track on SHOT CALLERS has its own distinct feel. On S.W.I.S.H. , you can hear how the tracks connect to each other. Woojin added that it is “an album with a really fun musical attitude.”

S.W.I.S.H. marks both LNGSHOT’s growth and a turning point for the group. Ahead of its release, Billboard Korea sat down with LNGSHOT for an exclusive interview.

Since September, you’ve been special guests on Jay Park’s world tour SERENADES & BODY ROLLS. How did it feel to perform for overseas audiences, and are there any moments that stand out?

Woojin: I remember that a lot of Louis’s family came to our show in France. We were also lucky to tour with Jay Park for two months, and every show sold out except in one city. The crowds were so responsive, and that gave us a lot of strength. Early on after our debut there was so much to worry about. But the more we performed and the more the audience responded, the more relaxed we got, and we could just have fun. We really enjoyed it. We’re the first idol group Jay Park has created, so I think when we look back later, these two months on the road with him as special guests will feel like a one-of-a-kind moment.

Ryul: I think I learned how to enjoy myself on stage. He also passed on a lot of know-how, like fan service, how to treat fans, and how to handle a busy schedule. He taught us how to take care of our mental health and how to stay mentally strong. We were preparing our comeback while touring, so we matured in some ways, and we learned a lot about what we need to do on stage and going forward.

How did you balance the tour with preparing for your comeback?

Woojin: Even before the tour, we kept making songs whenever we had time. In July and August, before we left, we sorted out all the songs, re-recorded them, and revised every part. During the tour, we shot the music video overseas, changed the choreography, and did more recording. Funnily enough, “Bananas” is a demo we’d been considering since before our debut.

entertainment.title: Eminem Releases ‘Infinite’ EP on Streaming & 30th Anniversary Documentary Surrounding His Debut Album
entertainment.summary: New mixes and additional production have been added to the project, which will be sold as physicals as well.
entertainment.body:
Long before the days of meeting Dr. Dre , Eminem was inspired by the likes of 2Pac and Nas when recording his debut album, Infinite , which arrived exactly 30 years ago on Thursday (Nov. 12).

Em celebrated the 30th anniversary of his independent release by bringing an EP version of the project to streaming services for the first time, which features six of the LP’s 11 songs: “Infinite,” “It’s O.K.,” “Tonite,” “313,” “Open Mic” and “Never 2 Far.”

Physical editions of Infinite are available at Org Music , with vinyl, CD and cassette options available for pre-order; they will arrive Feb. 26. Jake Bass and Mike “Slim” Wilde provide new mixes and additional production to the project.

Org Music also released a 10-minute documentary celebrating Infinite ‘s anniversary, featuring interviews with key players such as the Bass Brothers as well as Eminem, and archival footage from the mid-’90s era surrounding the project. (Watch the short film above.)

“After the Infinite release, we ended up [giving] the rest of the CDs and cassettes that didn’t sell just going to the places we could give ’em out,” Em recalls in the minidoc after selling less than 100 copies in ’96.

Released by WEB Entertainment, the album’s 1996 arrival didn’t bring Eminem the commercial breakthrough and radio success he had originally hoped for. Mark and Jeff of the Bass Brothers took Em under their wing and invested in the Detroit rapper, allowing him and other future members of D12 to record at their Bassmint studio. Mark saw the vision for Eminem, while Jeff just didn’t get it at the time. Infinite ‘s production was helmed by Em and Denaun Porter.

However, it all began to change when Em stopped making music seeking validation and dropped his filter to lean into his Slim Shady alter ego heading into 1997’s The Slim Shady EP, which caught the attention of Dr. Dre.

“As soon as I stopped giving a f — k about what I was saying, people started giving a f — k. It was like a reverse effect,” Eminem says in the short film.

Halloween might be over, but the “All’s Fair” actress is still dressing the part as she promotes the second season of her Hulu show. The latest? An ultra-rare high-fashion nurse outfit.

Among a carousel of images of Kardashian sporting a rare crocodile Hermès jacket, her Ashi Studio lace corset dress and more, the Calabasas native posed in the ultra-rare look from a Marc Jacobs-designed 2008 Louis Vuitton collection.

entertainment.title: Duran Duran Drummer Roger Taylor Stepping Down From Band Due to Tinnitus Diagnosis: ‘I Move On With Enormous Pride’
entertainment.summary: The timekeeper who has been with the new wave group since 1980 honored by his bandmates, whose drumming they said helped "define" their sound.
entertainment.body:
Longtime Duran Duran drummer Roger Taylor announced on Thursday (Nov. 12) that he is stepping down from the legendary new wave group after 46 years due to a recent diagnosis of tinnitus. In a statement , Taylor said he’s both retiring from Duran Duran and from playing the drums after keeping time with the act for nearly half a century.

“This is one of the hardest decisions I’ve ever had to make,” Taylor, 66, said in a statement. “Playing drums in this band has been the joy of my life, and I’ll never be able to properly thank the fans for the love they’ve shown us over the years. But the truth is that my tinnitus has been getting steadily worse, and I’ve reached the point where I must now listen to my body and my doctors.”

Taylor said figuring out the timing of his retirement from playing has been challenging, but that he feels he’s going out on top. “We’ve just returned from a hugely successful U.K. and European tour, which followed our second headline show at BST Hyde Park, our induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, and a return to the studio with Nile Rodgers,” he said. “I couldn’t have asked for a better final chapter, with so many special moments that I’ll treasure forever. I move on with enormous pride, and with nothing but love for [bandmates] Simon [Le Bon], Nick [Rhodes] and John [Taylor].”

According to the Mayo Clinic , tinnitus is a common condition that affects 15%-30% of people and is marked by a persistent ringing or noise inside one or both ears. It is often tied to age-related hearing loss, but can also result from an injury or the kind of regular exposure to loud sounds that are part of live performance and studio recording.

Taylor joined Duran Duran two years after the group was formed in Birmingham, England by original singer/bassist Stephen Duffy, keyboardist Nick Rhodes and guitarist/bassist John Taylor; by 1980, the band’s lineup had switched up to include singer Simon Le Bon, guitarist Andy Taylor and drummer Taylor. The legendary New Romantic group’s early videos for songs including “Planet Earth,” “Girls on Film,” “Hungry Like the Wolf” and “Rio” were staples of then-emerging video outlet MTV and stood out for their lush settings, occasional female nudity and high production values.

Taylor performed with the group from 1979-1985, then again when the original lineup got back together in 2001 through this year. He appeared on their crucial early albums, including 1981’s self-titled debut, 1982’s Rio and 1983’s Seven and the Ragged Tiger . He did not appear on the band’s late 1980s and early 1990s efforts, returning to play on a few tracks on their 1995 covers album Thank You and then officially rejoining in the studio for 2004’s Astronaut and five more LPs since, including 2023’s Danse Macabre .

entertainment.title: English Soccer Star Jude Bellingham Reveals He Can’t Drive or Cook

entertainment.body:
Jude Bellingham may be one of the greatest footballers of his generation.

But as it turns out, Team England’s star midfielder’s basic everyday skills—or lack thereof—help level the playing field, bringing him closer to us mere mortals.

“There’s loads of things I don’t know how to do,” Bellingham told British Vogue in an interview published Nov. 10 . “I can’t cook, I can’t drive. I’m good at what I do, but everything else? Not that great. I rely on my friends, my family to help me do stuff—chef, cleaner, mum, whoever else. That’s where I’m at.”

In fact, he’s been so busy keeping his eye on the literal ball—and doing a really good job at it—he may have lost track of life’s other skills.

“I work hard every day and all day, and then when I get home,” the 23-year-old said, “I’ve probably neglected learning how to do some of the more basic things.”

In his defense, not only is learning those life skills par for the course for many early twenty-somethings, but Bellingham’s daytime job also takes up a lot of his time.

“I feel mature in a football context because I’ve played nearly 400 games,” he reflected. “But in a life context I don’t feel that mature now, to be honest.”

entertainment.title: Eminem’s Debut Release ‘Infinite’ Now Streaming for 30th Anniversary
entertainment.summary: Originally a full, independently released album, Infinite EP features six songs remixed with new production
entertainment.body:
Eminem ‘s independently released debut album, Infinite , bombed when it came out 30 years ago today. “It sold maybe 70 copies and didn’t get great feedback,” he wrote in his 2008 memoir, The Way I Am . “A lot of people said it sounded like Nas, and he was a heavy influence at the time. But I had an album out, and I could say that.” Since then, the album has taken on a legend of its own, since it caught the ears of Dr. Dre and led to Marshall Mathers’ breakthrough Slim Shady LP . The album has been reissued and bootlegged for years.

Now Infinite is getting another chance as an EP. Jake Bass and Mike “Slim” Wilder have remixed and added additional production to six of the album’s original 11 tracks for what’s now called Infinite EP . Jeff and Mark Bass, who helmed the original release, executive produced the EP, which Denaun Porter produced with Wilder. The EP is now available to stream and physical editions, which will come out on vinyl, CD, and tape on Feb. 26, can be pre-ordered . It’s unclear at the time of publication why only half of the album is being re-released.

Org Music has also produced a 10-minute documentary about the album. Jeff Bass recalls in the film how his brother Mark heard Eminem do an open mic on the radio and called the station to get the rapper to the studio. The brothers recall how Eminem showed up with D12 and started recording. There’s also archival footage of Eminem and stories from others who helped make the record.

entertainment.title: Karin Slaughter Said “Absolutely Not” to Adapting Her Novel ‘The Good Daughter.’ Then She Wrote the Whole Series
entertainment.summary: The bestselling novelist initially turned down Bruna Papandrea, wrote all six episodes of the Peacock series on her own and only then pitched it: "I wanted to make sure I could land the plane."
entertainment.body:
Logo text Some stories refuse to stay on the page. The Hollywood Reporter’ s Beyond the Book column explores what happens when books make the leap to screen and beyond — unpacking what stayed, changed, how it was done and why it matters with the creatives who made it.

When producer Bruna Papandrea asked whether she’d be interested in bringing one of her novels to the screen herself, the author’s answer was immediate. “I said, ‘Absolutely not,’” Slaughter tells The Hollywood Reporter. “I don’t have time.” Related Stories TV 'The Good Daughter' Review: Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy Elevate Peacock's Overly Familiar Southern-Fried Thriller General News Foundation Books Unveils First Titles in Macmillan Partnership; John Goodman to Narrate Animated Short Adaptation (Exclusive)

She’d already watched two of her books become hits in other hands: Netflix’s Pieces of Her , adapted by Charlotte Stoudt, and ABC’s Will Trent , run by Liz Heldens. Though she declined, Slaughter couldn‘t move on, and the idea that she might do it herself stuck. So she started writing the scripts, and she told no one.

“I wrote them completely on my own because I didn’t want to tell anybody if I’d done a bad job,” she tells THR . When she finally told her agent, she made one request: Don’t tell Papandrea — or anyone for that matter — yet. “Because she’d want an option. I just wanted to do this in secret.”

The secrecy also gave her time to take on the creative challenge. “I know from my novel writing that the beginning of a story is important, but just as important is the end,” she says. “People can read a book they think is mediocre, and that’s fine. But if it starts out really great and craps out at the end, they’re furious. So I wanted to make sure I could land the plane.”

With the scripts done, Slaughter went back to Papandrea. “I said to Bruna, ‘This is the show. If you’re interested, that’s great. If not, obviously I’ll take notes, but I haven’t wasted your time and money on an option.’ She read it overnight and said, ‘Let’s go, let’s do this.’”

The result is The Good Daughter , Peacock’s six-episode adaptation of Slaughter’s 2017 bestseller, which drops on the streamer in full on Nov. 12. Slaughter is the sole writer on every episode and serves as showrunner and executive producer.

The series stars Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy as Samantha and Charlotte Quinn, sisters still living with the aftermath of a single event of violence during their childhood, with Brendan Gleeson as their father, Rusty. The cast also includes Shayna Benardo, Olivia Williams, Harper Steele, Jake McDorman and Michael Dorman. Made Up Stories, Papandrea’s banner, produces with Fifth Season.

entertainment.title: How ‘Godmother of K-Culture’ Miky Lee Earned the Asian Hall of Fame’s Centennial Medal of Lifetime Achievement
entertainment.summary: As CJ Group vice chair, Lee helped launch Superstar K , the MAMA Awards and KCON, making K-pop a global phenomenon.
entertainment.body:
CJ Group Vice Chair Miky Lee has received the Centennial Medal of Lifetime Achievement from the Asian Hall of Fame during an awards ceremony in Los Angeles, which took place on Nov. 5. The honor shows how Lee has steadily built major milestones for both Korean film and K-pop over the years.

The Asian Hall of Fame is a cross-cultural educational and research institution dedicated to recognizing Asian and Indigenous legacy, early-career achievement and interracial collaboration. In a given year, the Centennial Medal of Lifetime Achievement goes to only a handful of people, and recipients are chosen from figures who have built decades of global achievement and influence in fields such as culture, arts and entertainment. That sets the medal apart from the annual Class Inductees, which comprise a larger group of people.

The award carries particular weight because it recognizes Lee’s role over the past 30-odd years as a bridge between Korea and the world. Throughout her career, she has widened the base for the global spread of Korean content and exchange between cultures. Billboard Korea takes a look back at what Lee has done to help build K-pop’s global infrastructure, and at what the Centennial Medal of Lifetime Achievement means.

While Lee’s name is familiar in the film world, she stated during her acceptance speech in Los Angeles on Nov. 5 that music was the starting point. “And me? I simply loved music,” she said, adding that music “has been at the heart of everything we’ve built in culture.” Lee is the figure who created and developed K-pop’s anchor points, building on music platforms that span broadcasting, distribution and live performance.

The origin of the “K-survival audition,” a cradle for K-pop talent

On July 24, 2009, Mnet’s Superstar K first went on air, raising the curtain on Korea’s first modern survival audition show. It went on to produce a long list of standout stars, and countless audition programs followed the show’s model. Lee had been the one to initially suggest that Mnet look into a program of its own after she had taken note of American Idol in the U.S.

In 2016, Mnet’s Produce 101 carried the audition format over into idol survival and set off another craze. The Produce series went on to launch I.O.I, Wanna One and IZ*ONE. Boys Planet series gave rise to ZEROBASEONE and ALPHA DRIVE ONE, and I-LAND2 produced izna.

The stage didn’t stop at Korea. In Japan, the PRODUCE 101 JAPAN series formed JO1, INI and ME:I, and KO1KEYZ debuted through 2026’s PRODUCE 101 JAPAN SHINSEKAI . Today, CJ ENM’s local label business in Japan is broadening its scope beyond audition-linked groups, extending to the development of Japanese boy band DXTEEN.

entertainment.title: Stephen Miller Wants to Win Back Young Men. It Might Not Be So Easy
entertainment.summary: The demographic has swung left to a staggering degree since Donald Trump's 2024 election win
entertainment.body:
Stephen Miller is not much of a man, at least by the right wing’s increasingly Herculean standards. Gawky, bald, and pasty, Miller has nevertheless ascended during Donald Trump’s second administration, most recently climbing from an advisory role to the lame-duck leader’s chief of staff .

In that role, Axios reports , Miller has one priority: win back America’s young men to the MAGA cause.

The right sees young men as one of its most important demographics , as they have been less susceptible to the overall leftward shift of young people over the past 20 years. But after making massive gains with the group in the 2024 cycle, Trump’s MAGA Man project stumbled, its support drying up faster than the lawn in front of a Texas frat house. In the 2026 midterms , young men swung 38 points in favor of the Democrats compared to how they voted in 2024. Why this happened is a complex puzzle, but the biggest piece in it is clear: American men are sick of war. In Iran, they faced the existential threat that America would revert to the warlike nation that sucked their older brothers’ and parents’ generation into 20 years of futile bloodshed in the Middle East.

Miller appears to have identified this early. The New York Times reported last week that Miller’s pitch to Trump when he was angling for the chief of staff job involved direct advice to wind down the Iran war, which Miller thought — correctly — had alienated supporters he couldn’t afford to lose.

But Iran is only part of the picture. I’ve reported on masculinity in America for years, and the anxieties that young voters face are more holistic than just a fear of being sent to die in a foreign land. That’s part of it, of course — while Generation Z was mostly too young to fight in the peak of the Global War on Terror, plenty of them remember older siblings or parents who spent years away in Iraq or Afghanistan. But what they remember even more were the economic effects of 20 years of American war. For many young men I’ve spoken to over the past few years, their childhood political memories aren’t Clinton getting a blowjob or the all-encompassing trauma of 9/11. Those on the older side remember their parents losing jobs in the 2008 crash; those on the younger side left high school or college and walked right into the Covid pandemic. Sanders reports to BMI vp, creative, Nashville Clay Bradley .

Michelle .

Prior to joining BMI, Sanders founded and served as program director at Nashville’s 102.1 The Ville and worked as co-musical director for the Fisk Jubilee Singers and India.Arie. Sanders has earned three Grammy Awards, three Emmys, a GMA Dove Award and was honored with the Academy of Country Music’s Lifting Lives Award in 2024. The National Museum of African American Music honored him as a Living Legend in 2025, and he was inducted into Tennessee State University’s Hall of Fame for Distinguished Alumni. He continues to be active in industry organizations including the Recording Academy and Leadership Music, and serves on the boards of the ACM, Americana Music Association, Country Music Association, International Bluegrass Music Association and more.

“Shannon’s extensive industry experience and unwavering commitment to songwriters make him an invaluable member of BMI’s Creative team,” Bradley said in a statement. “He’s been a constant champion of Nashville’s diverse music community, honoring its rich heritage while creating new opportunities for writers across all genres. Shannon has also helped to expand and strengthen BMI’s programs and relationships, and I look forward to working with him to build on that success.”

entertainment.summary: NBC Sports announcer Dan Hicks died November 11 following an acute illness at the age of 64. His wife, ESPN's Hannah Storm, has released a statement.
entertainment.body:
Dan Hicks, the longtime NBC Sports announcer whose voice accompanied some of the biggest moments in golf and Olympic history, died November 11 following an acute illness. He was 64.

"Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan," Hicks' wife, ESPN anchor Hannah Storm, shared in a statement . "He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many. His loss is immeasurable.

"Dan was truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around," her statement continued. "When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter and the people together. He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered. Our three daughters and I are heartbroken. We are grateful for the love and support surrounding our family during this incredibly difficult time. There are simply no words to express how much he will be missed."

NBC Sports chief Rick Cordella, and veteran executives Sam Flood and Molly Solomon, also released a joint statement : "Dan Hicks was an extraordinary colleague, friend and person. In his 34 years at NBC Sports, he was an exceptional storyteller and caller of games and events who elevated some of the biggest moments in sports history. From Olympic swimming and skiing to Notre Dame football, numerous other high profile events and especially as the signature voice of our golf coverage for the last 26 years, Dan's blend of knowledge, style, enthusiasm and humor informed and entertained fans for decades. But far beyond his on-air excellence, Dan was a better person who welcomed teammates with a smile, a joke, or a word of encouragement, sometimes all three in the same sentence. Our heartfelt condolences and love to his wife Hannah and his daughters Hannah, Ellery, and Riley."

Following a three-year stint at CNN, Hicks joined NBC Sports in 1992 and became the network's lead golf play-by-play announcer in 2000. He also handled play-by-play at 15 Olympic Games — including eight Summer Olympics as a swimming commentator, and four consecutive Winter Olympics calling Alpine skiing. His other assignments included Notre Dame football, the NFL, NBA, and French Open tennis.

Among Hicks' most memorable calls was Tiger Woods' dramatic putt to force a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open ("Expect anything different?"). Two months later, he called all eight of Michael Phelps' gold medals at the Beijing Olympics. In all, Hicks called each of Phelps' 28 Olympic medals between 2004 and 2016.

entertainment.title: Az Cohen’s New AZTEC Label Signs First Artist
entertainment.summary: The label’s debut artist, Beeson, from Arizona, will release her first single under for AZTEC on Dec. 4.
entertainment.body:
AZTEC, the new independent label founded by Az Cohen as a joint venture with French music giant Believe, has signed its first artist: Beeson , an indie pop singer-songwriter from Arizona.

Beeson has been releasing music on her own since 2023, the year she graduated from BYU, and has been building a fan base through more than 100 shows around the state of Utah during that period. She released her first EP, Last Shot , in 2023 and her second, Ritual , in 2025; her latest single, “Going,” came out in July. Beeson’s first release for AZTEC will be the song “Worse Not Better,” due out Dec. 4.

“AZTEC was founded with a laser focus on finding super-powered humans with a real sense of who they are and what they want,” Cohen, the son of YouTube global head of music Lyor Cohen , said in a statement about the new signing. “Beeson knows with clarity what things are supposed to look like, sound like, feel like, taste like and even smell like in the universe she is cultivating. Ultimately it is our privilege to support her in the everyday work that goes into building that out. She is one of the most powerful songwriters I’ve had the good fortune of working with. My team and I are so excited to show up and relentlessly share her gift with the world.”

Cohen founded AZTEC earlier this year after leaving 300 Entertainment, the once-indie label now owned by the Warner Music Group at which he spent more than a decade building out his A&R experience and working with artists such as Young Thug , Gunna and more. He was involved in Post Malone ’s early career as well, and eventually took over 300’s distribution engine Sparta, which he ran until founding AZTEC.

The JV also notably marks Believe’s first label venture in the United States, after the company established itself firmly with divisions around the world over the past 20 years, having made the foray into the world’s largest music market in 2026. And now, Beeson is the first artist signed to Believe’s first U.S. label.

“I’ve always dreamt of landing with a team that could give my project a limitless ceiling while I hold the reins, and working with AZTEC has shown that I can truly have both, and have a good time while I’m at it,” Beeson said in a statement. “I’ve been totally indie up until now, and the thing that drew me to this team is that they are both scrappy and super legit. They aren’t afraid to get their hands dirty, but they know how to play in the big leagues because each of them already has. The squad is made up of humans who are both specialists and jacks of all trades; they are each true experts in their fields, but seriously down to help with whatever I need, whenever, the way you have to when you’re building something from the ground up. It feels really special to be working with a crew this dedicated, and I’m stoked for what we’re building together.”

entertainment.title: Ms. Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean to Celebrate 30 Years of ‘The Score’ With Art Basel Performance
entertainment.summary: The cultural platform's launch event is set for Florida's Faena Forum in December.
entertainment.body:
Ms. Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean will continue the 30th anniversary celebration of the Fugees’ The Score album with a performance at the launch of Saint & Citizen’s The Fourth Space at Art Basel in Miami Beach, Fla.

Set for the Faena Forum on Dec. 5 in the midst of Miami Art Week, The Fourth Space serves as a new cultural platform featuring an immersive art exhibition, a performance from Lauryn Hill and Wyclef, and conversations exploring the intersection of art, migration, storytelling and The Score .

“Home is our first space, work our second and the places we gather our third. The Fourth Space is the one we create through shared culture, memory and experience. Thirty years ago, The Score gave a generation shaped by migration a language for identity, belonging and possibility,” said Saint & Citizen CEO Paula Grant in a statement. “To honor Ms. Lauryn Hill alongside Wyclef Jean in Miami, a city whose identity has been shaped by generations of people bringing their cultures with them, feels especially fitting.”

She continued: “It speaks to the heart of why Saint & Citizen exists: to close the distance between those who shape culture and those whose lives are shaped by it. To create spaces where culture isn’t simply witnessed, but shared, experienced and lived.”

Registration for early access tickets is now open on the Saint & Citizen website. The Dec. 5 exibition will open at 12 p.m. ET, while the performance from the Fugees members is set for 8 p.m. ET through 10 p.m. ET. An afterparty will continue the festivities with various DJs spinning sets to close the night.

Released in February 1996, The Score is the Fugees’ second and final album to date. The sophomore LP, which was nominated for album of the year and won for best rap album at the 1997 Grammys, debuted atop the Billboard 200.

Lauryn Hill and Wyclef hit the stage together earlier this year, when the duo reunited for a rare South American performance at Global Citizen Live: Rio De Janeiro in June.

Weeks later, Hill was honored with the Living Legend Icon Award at the 2026 BET Awards, which was preceded with a spectacular medley performance paying homage to the Grammy winner’s legacy featuring The War and Treaty , Doechii and SZA , Tems and Tierra Whack , Doja Cat , Nas , Hill’s sons YG and Zion Marley, Lizzo , Alexia Jayy , Queen Latifah and Common .

entertainment.title: ‘Ebenezer’ Review: Johnny Depp Gets a Creepily Effective Comeback Vehicle in Ti West’s Horror-Tinged Take on Dickens’ Yuletide Classic
entertainment.summary: The film's supporting cast includes Ian McKellen, Daisy Ridley, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Tramell Tillman and Rupert Grint.
entertainment.body:
Did the world need another cinematic adaptation of Charles Dickens’ classic A Christmas Carol ? Not really, considering the myriad versions that have appeared over the years, which play with regularity on television screens every holiday season. But Johnny Depp really needed a comeback vehicle, and he’s found an effective one in Ti West ’s horror-tinged adaptation that allows the actor to deliver the sort of quirky theatrical performance for which he became famous. While Ebenezer doesn’t break any new ground, other than possibly being the first version of the story not really suitable for young children, it fulfills its ostensible goal of restoring the actor to A-list status. Related Stories Movies Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer': First Reactions Movies AFM Hot Project: Daisy Ridley, Sosie Bacon, Simon Rex Join 'Get Rid of It'

Considering that the director’s oeuvre consists of such films as The House of the Devil , Cabin Fever 2: Spring Fever , and the recent acclaimed X trilogy, it’s not surprising that this version of the Yuletide tale features a dark Gothic tone. Indeed, Ebenezer feels essentially like a horror film for most of its running time, featuring jump scares, grotesque visuals, and enough ghostly creatures to fuel a season of American Horror Story . It’s no wonder a terrified Scrooge pees himself at one point. Ebenezer The Bottom Line Gets the ghostly job done. Release date : Friday, November 13 Cast : Johnny Depp, Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley, Arthur Conti, Ellie Bamber, Henry Lloyd-Hughes, Charlie Murphy, Tramell Tillman, Ian McKellen Director : Ti West Screenwriter : Nathaniel Halpern Rated PG-13, 1 hour 56 minutes

Still, plenty of care has been taken for the movie, which features handsome visuals, excellent production design, and a stacked cast including Ian McKellen as Scrooge’s business partner Jacob Marley. Nathaniel Halpern’s screenplay expands upon the tale by providing more backstory than usual, with Marley still alive in the pre-credits prologue and demonstrating that he was just as irascible and nasty as Scrooge.

Cut to seven years later, when Scrooge is at his most Scrooge-like, uttering enough humbugs to satisfy those Dickens fans. (Another nod to them is that the film is divided into “staves,” as was the author’s novella.)

Soon enough, Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his former partner, who, besides carrying those infernal chains, looks decidedly worse for wear. Marley warns him that he’ll soon be visited by three ghosts who will … wait, why am I relating the story? You already know it.

entertainment.title: You Can’t See Everything: The Sneaky Problem With the Elizabeth Holmes Documentary
entertainment.summary: The Fielder-Oppemheim movie is a sensation thanks to the directors’ layering of multiple and competing truths. But are they dangerously furthering an anti-fact culture?
entertainment.body:
Logo text More than 100 years ago, a filmmaker directed the first documentary . Controversy has followed the form ever since.

Nanook of the North , Robert Flaherty’s Inuit vérité, redefined way back in 1922 how we imagined cinema, but critics in subsequent decades charged him with staging scenes, sensationalizing events and substituting actors for real people.

In the 1980s, Errol Morris disrupted the doc world with The Thin Blue Line , his reexamination of a Texas murder case from a decade earlier. So compellingly did Morris interrogate the incident that it led to an overturned conviction — but prompted a whole new inquest into why he reconstructed scenes. Two decades later, Michael Moore dropped the grenade of Fahrenheit 9/11 . The look at George W. Bush’s foreign policy sins brought Americans to the theaters by the millions but generated heat for what Moore exaggerated or left out. Related Stories Movies 'One in a Million' Filmmaker on the Ethical Dilemma He Faced and Learning to Let His Subject Find Her Own Way Movies Amanda Seyfried Feared 'You Can See Everything' Could "Destroy" Her Career, Says Her Opinion of Billy Evans "Only Got Worse"

Yet something feels different with this decade’s documentary sensation, which doesn’t just play fast and loose with the truth, but plays fast and loose with the truth while making the truth the very subject of its inquiry. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s observational Elizabeth Holmes doc You Can See Everything , ostensibly about how much Holmes and her husband Billy Evans are lying, has already solicited the kind of box office dollars more familiar to midbudget thrillers, becoming the non-fiction film world’s buzziest pop-cultural phenomenon since a posthumous Michael Jackson rehearsal doc in 2009. Like its forebears, YCSE leaves itself open to questions about manipulation, starting with the fact that two camera setups followed every supposedly unselfconscious reaction, and the fact that Holmes initiated the project, possibly with crisis PR specialist Risa Heller, who helped place a soft interview in The New York Times at around the same time. I suspect the coming months will bring more objections of the sort.

But this time the skepticism goes beyond fears of subject-nudging and selective editing. The entire YCSE project is built by people who specialize in presenting falsehoods as truth, each layer composed by someone whose very brand is deception, like a grift-y cinematic lasagna.

entertainment.title: The Wild Stories Behind Trapped Under Ice’s 2007 Demo
entertainment.summary: Check out an excerpt from Flatspot Records' upcoming book, Intent to Distribute: Twenty Years of Flatspot Records
entertainment.body:
Almost 20 years ago, Baltimore ’s Trapped Under Ice released their first demo — a record that would sow the seeds, in many ways, of modern hardcore . After all, it launched the career of one of the genre’s most dynamic frontmen, Justice Tripp of Angel Du$t , and later featured Turnstile ‘s Brendan Yates on drums.

Now, the story behind the creation of that demo has finally been told — via the upcoming book “Intent to Distribute: Twenty Years of Flatspot Records,” out Feb. 5, 2027 . The book, written by journalist Fred Pessaro, contains exclusive photos, artwork, and interviews with bands that the label launched, including Tripp, Backtrack, Terror, Speed, End It, and Scowl. Rolling Stone has the first excerpt, about TUI’s demo, below.

“When you spend so much time doing something, you’re usually focused on what’s next. You’re putting out the next record, planning the next campaign, working on the next show,” says label co-founder Ricky Singh. “You don’t always stop to look at everything that’s happened along the way. Making this book gave us an opportunity to do that. It’s a collection of people, bands, friendships and experiences that have shaped Flatspot over the last 20 years.”

Adds co-founder Che Figueroa-Rodriguez: “Throughout the last 20 years there has been a lot of blood and sweat and the driving force that carried us through every era of the label was that same passion we had when we started.”

That passion will be on full display at an anniversary show on Feb. 6 at New York’s Webster Hall, featuring performances by Trapped Under Ice, Breakdown, End It, Raw Brigade, Iron Mind, and Frothing Mad.

The Breakdown and Outburst demos in ’87. Beyond’s Dew it! and Turning Point’s demo in ’88. Merauder’s ’93 demo. All signs point toward Trapped Under Ice’s 2007 demo being named in the same breath as some of these legendary early efforts. Depending on the era, it’s quite possible that the record known as FSR02 could go down as the single most important hardcore demo of all time. Flatspot Records proudly released this five-song monster on vinyl after witnessing its creation in Joe Mitra’s basement so many years ago, and it has remained a crucial part of the catalog ever since. The record, initially paid for in stolen goods and later pressed with drug money, proved to be not only a major landmark for hardcore in the Mid-Atlantic, but for the genre writ large, causing a monolithic shift in sound and style. entertainment.title: The Rings Of Power Season 3 Killed Off A Major Tolkien Character Off-Screen
entertainment.summary: The third season of Amazon Prime Video's "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" is taking no prisoners when it comes to character deaths.
entertainment.body:
Ben Rothstein/Prime Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 3 – "The Secret Fire"

In "The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 3 , the Secret Fire reveals to Gandalf (Daniel Weyman) that the long-anticipated second Blue Wizard in Rhûn died before the "Rings of Power" story started — seconds after the character is first revealed in a flashback. Season 3 has delivered some shocking deaths that no one saw coming , and this one was another surprise.

In the rapid-fire scene, we learn that the Dark Wizard (Ciarán Hinds) is Pallando, one of Tolkien's two Blue Wizards. We also find out that Pallando betrayed and murdered his erstwhile companion (presumably Alatar, the other Blue Wizard). The vile event is even credited as the very act that turned Rhûn into a desert.

It's important to remember that this part of Gandalf's story is being invented for the show. Tolkien never wrote about Gandalf being in Middle-earth during the Second Age — or traveling in the eastern regions of Rhûn, for that matter. But the connection between the Wizard and the Secret Fire is vintage Tolkienian lore and goes right back to Gandalf's confrontation with the Balrog in the author's original writings.

In the Amazon show, the hot holy presence first appears to Gandalf out in the deserts of Rhûn. And if you're wondering what this strange burning presence is in the first place, the Secret Fire is a vague term Tolkien uses to represent the creative power of Ilúvatar, the monotheistic, God-like Creator of his world. As the author writes early in "The Silmarillion," "The Secret Fire was sent to burn at the heart of the World; and it was called Eä."

Prime Video The Dark Wizard entered the "Rings of Power" story in Season 2 and remained an important plot point to remember heading into Season 3 . Fans particularly wanted to know if he was one of J.R.R. Tolkien's enigmatic Blue Wizards from Rhûn. Showrunners JD Payne and Patrick McKay all but confirmed this during Season 2. All that was left for Season 3 was to confirm the character and show us where the other Blue Wizard, Alatar, was hiding. The thought that the Dark Wizard's partner was already long gone, killed by his own Wizarding friend, wasn't on most people's bingo cards. That's partly because Tolkien doesn't say anything about one of the Wizards killing the other, nor is there any indication that their specific behavior is the reason Rhûn is a desert wasteland.

The Bills lead the all-time series 73-58, have won five straight against New York and own a 10-2 record against the Jets since 2020. Buffalo has also kept New York out of the end zone on its opening drive in each of their last 25 meetings. It’s been a while since the Jets have given Bills fans much reason to worry. Of course, when two teams have been playing each other twice a year for decades, there’s only so much history we can dig up before we start telling the same stories. And while we’re always happy to revisit a good Bills win, even our Time Capsule could use a change of scenery. Head coach Aaron Glenn, defensive coordinator Brian Duker and offensive coordinator Frank Reich all have some history with Buffalo. They’ve faced Allen, coached against the Bills and, in Reich’s case, even worn a Buffalo uniform. Glenn already has a season with the Jets under his belt, while Duker and Reich are getting their first taste of this rivalry from New York’s sideline. But none of them is a stranger to Buffalo, and their previous encounters give us a few interesting games to revisit. _____________________________________________________________________________ Aaron Glenn has seen plenty of Josh Allen Aaron Glenn is in his second season as the Jets’ head coach, but his history with Josh Allen goes back to his four seasons as defensive coordinator for the Detroit Lions. And if Glenn was hoping a change of teams would make Allen any easier to deal with, the results so far haven’t offered much encouragement. The two first met on Thanksgiving Day in 2022, when Buffalo traveled to Detroit and came away with a 28-25 victory. Allen threw for 253 yards and two touchdowns, added another 78 yards and a touchdown on the ground, and helped set up Tyler Bass’s game-winning field goal with a 36-yard completion to Stefon Diggs in the final seconds. Detroit entered the game at 12-1, riding an 11-game winning streak and looking every bit like a Super Bowl contender. But Allen wasn’t particularly impressed. sports.title: Report: Chiefs, 49ers showed interest in trading for Garrett Wilson
sports.summary: The Chiefs and 49ers both traded for a receiver at this week's deadline, as Kansas City acquired Josh Downs and San Francisco brought in Keenan Allen.
sports.body:
Per Rich Cimini of ESPN, both the Chiefs and 49ers showed interest in the Jets’ Garrett Wilson.

But, as Cimini notes, Wilson did not want to leave New York and the club did not want to trade Wilson, who’s arguably the team’s best player. The Jets view Wilson, who is under contract through 2030, as a foundational piece.

Wilson, the No. 10 overall pick of the 2022 draft, agreed to a four-year, $130 million deal in July. The Jets had previously exercised Wilson’s fifth-year option in April.

After registering over 1,000 yards in each of his first three seasons, injuries limited Wilson to just seven games last season. He caught 36 passes for 395 yards with four touchdowns.

In eight games so far in 2026, Wilson has 43 receptions for 527 yards with three TDs.

sports.title: 49ers pivoted to Keenan Allen trade after initially focusing on Josh Downs
sports.summary: The 49ers made a trade for wide receiver Keenan Allen on Tuesday, but he wasn't the only Colts wide receiver on their radar ahead of the trade deadline.
sports.body:
During a Thursday appearance on KNBR, General Manager John Lynch said that the team turned its attention to Allen after initially targeting Josh Downs as an addition to their receiver room. Lynch said that head coach Kyle Shanahan brought up Allen while watching film on Downs and conversations with the Colts began before they landed defensive tackle DeForest Buckner in an earlier deal with Indianapolis.

“We kind of focused on Josh Downs as an option that we’d have some interest,” Lynch said, via 49ersWebzone.com. “And Kyle and I are kind of watching Josh, and in the process, Kyle’s like, ‘Man, what about Keenan?’ And I was like, ‘You know, we hadn’t given much thought to that, but let me ask about that.’ And so, there started a conversation about two and a half weeks ago, really, when the DeForest talks [happened]. ‘Would he?’ And it’s always fluid, and at a certain time, they didn’t want to give up Keenan. It kind of wasn’t going to be on the table, but we kept communicating, and ultimately we got him.”

The 49ers sent a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Colts for Allen. Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick were eventually traded to the Chiefs for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks.

sports.title: Lions vs. Patriots matches up this year's two most aggressive head coaches on fourth downs
sports.summary: When the Lions meet the Patriots in Munich on Sunday, the fans in Germany are likely to see both teams go for it on fourth down.
sports.body:
That’s because Lions head coach Dan Campbell has long been the league’s most aggressive coach on fourth downs, and this year, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel is No. 2.

Coaches’ fourth down decisions are tracked for the Aggressiveness Index at FTN Fantasy, looking at how often coaches go for it compared to other coaches in the same situation. By that measurement, Campbell is first with a score of 1.45 (meaning he goes for it 45 percent more than an average NFL coach) and Vrabel is second with a score of 1.22.

The Aggressiveness Index is a more detailed way of tracking a coach’s fourth-down decision making than simply looking at the number of times a team has gone for it on fourth down. Some teams go for it often on fourth down not because the coach is aggressive, but because they happen to face a lot of fourth-and-shorts while trailing late in the fourth quarter. That’s not a particularly aggressive time to go for it.

What gives Campbell such a high score on the Aggressiveness Index is decisions like going for it on fourth down at his own 24-yard line with the score tied late in the fourth quarter against the Packers. That’s the kind of call that Campbell makes and other coaches don’t, which is why his Aggressiveness Index is so much higher than any other coach’s.

Campbell is at or near the top of the Aggressiveness Index every year. Last year he was second only to Mike Kafka , who was very aggressive on fourth downs during his seven-game stint as the Giants’ interim head coach. Perhaps unsurprisingly, after Kafka was not retained by the Giants, Campbell hired him to be the Lions’ passing game coordinator.

Vrabel has not been as aggressive as Campbell on fourth downs, but he has been more aggressive than the average NFL coach, both during his time with the Patriots and before that as head coach of the Titans. Both Vrabel and Campbell are former players with reputations for a blend of old-school toughness and a new-school understanding of the strategic advantages of aggressive fourth-down decision making. It’s a winning combination.

sports.title: PFT's Week 10 2026 NFL picks
sports.summary: I have no explanation for the last two weeks.
sports.body:
In Week 8, I went 13-1 in the straight-up-only picks exercise. (No more picks against the spread, for reasons I’ve previously explained.) For Week 9, I ended up 14-1.

That’s 27-2 over two weeks. (Which translates to 87-48-1 for the year, which doesn’t sound nearly as good as “27-2.”)

Now for the warning, specifically to anyone who has gambled or who will be gambling on sports. The worst thing you can do is get lucky. Because you’ll think that you’ve suddenly become good.

Then, you’ll let it ride until your luck runs out. That’s when it gets dangerous. Because you’ll fool yourself into thinking that it’s just a temporary setback, that your secret formula for picking winners remains viable, and you’ll chase your losses. You’ll keep digging that hole, confident that it’s just a matter of time before your sudden genius returns.

Eventually, you’ll find yourself in an untenable financial situation.

That’s how it happens for plenty of gamblers. They don’t start out losing and keep losing. They win enough to make themselves think they know more than they do, when the reality is that no one knows anything. And then the wheels come off. And then they get desperate to put the wheels back on.

Case in point: Last week, someone who has been part of the NFL universe for more than 30 years expressed amazement that the Cowboys were favored by only 4.5 points against the Colts. With the Colts in disarray due to multiple trades and poised to make even more trades, the Cowboys would win easily. It was, the person said, a “sure thing.”

There is no sure thing in gambling. Well, there’s one. If you ever let yourself believe you’re smarter than the house and you don’t snap out of it in time, it’s a sure thing that you’ll be filing for bankruptcy, eventually.

sports.title: Trevor Lawrence: Trades show the confidence in our team, what we have a chance to do
sports.summary: The Jaguars signaled they're all-in on the 2026 season by making several trades to fortify their roster before the deadline.
sports.body:
Quarterback Trevor Lawrence told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that the moves signal a positive trend for the team.

“I think you try not to look too much into it,” Lawrence said, via transcript from the team. “We have the same job to do, and I think we have a really good team that has good chemistry. Has gelled together. We like playing together, we have great camaraderie. All those things that are just hard to put your finger on sometimes. I think we have all that. I think we’ve been playing well, and so we still have a job to do, and nothing changes from that perspective.

“But I do think, obviously with the moves made, I think it shows the confidence in our team, and what we have the chance to do. I think that we’re a really good team, and now we get even better with these guys. I think that’s all it is, is just making our team even better, and we know that we’re going to have a shot. We just got to keep playing well and we got to keep winning. I think you can’t look too much into it because we still have the same job right in front of us, but I think these guys are going to help us for sure.”

Moreover, it helps that the players acquired have significant postseason experience.

“I think to get winners, to get guys that have been there before, that experience is important,” Lawrence said. “I think that is, why would you not want that if you can? Obviously, you got to look at the players you’re getting, and you want great players, but if they’ve also won Super Bowls and been to Super Bowls, I think that’s icing on the cake or whatever. That’s a plus. So, we have some guys obviously in that group that have done that. Just excited to get that experience. I think they’ve played meaningful football. They know what it looks like and going to add that value to our team.”

We’ll see how the additions start to fit in when the Jaguars play the Titans on Sunday.

sports.title: Longtime Steelers player, coach Dick Hoak dies at 86
sports.summary: The Steelers announced the death of their longtime player and coach Dick Hoak at the age of 86.
sports.body:
Hoak was born outside of Pittsburgh and went to Penn State before the Steelers made him a 1961 seventh-round pick. He spent 10 years as one of the team’s running backs and finished his career with 3,965 rushing yards and 1,452 receiving yards. Hoak scored 33 overall touchdowns during his time on the roster.

Hoak joined Chuck Noll’s staff as an offensive backfield coach in 1972, moved to running backs coach in 1991 and was the only one of Noll’s coaches who remained on the staff under Noll’s successor Bill Cowher. He retired in 2006 after coaching future Hall of Famers Franco Harris and Jerome Bettis and being part of five Super Bowl champions.

“We are deeply saddened by the passing of Dick Hoak, a legendary member of the Pittsburgh Steelers family,” Steelers owner Art Rooney II said in a statement. “Dick was part of the foundation of this organization and played an instrumental role in shaping the Steelers as both a player and coach during his 45 years with the team. Dick represented everything the Steelers stand for with his toughness, loyalty, dedication and an unwavering commitment to the team. First as a player, then as a coach, Dick’s contributions to this organization spanned generations.”

Hoak is a member of the Steelers’ Hall of Honor and received the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Award of Excellence in 2025.

“Obviously, having gone from the emergency quarterback at the beginning of the season to last week being the backup to now being the starter, it’s been a crazy season,” Beck said, via transcript from the team. “It’s really been a welcome to the NFL season, just getting introduced to what the league is and what it can be, but I’m super excited for the opportunity and to have the chance to go play with these guys.”

Beck will be the third starting quarterback for the Cardinals this season after Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew. Beck noted he’s picked up plenty from observing both veteran QBs to this point in the year.

“I think the biggest thing is just watching those two and how they carry themselves and how they handle themselves not only in the meeting room around the coaches, but during the walkthrough, during practice, and during the game,” Beck said. “I think that’s the biggest thing that you can learn from those guys, of everybody’s looking at you as a quarterback, and your attitude has to be right each and every day. The moxie [of] going out there, having confidence, and making everyone around you better.

“I think that’s something that I learned in how they carry themselves and when they went on the field — how I need to carry myself as well.”

To that end, Beck said “of course” he can maintain his sense of confidence entering Sunday.

“I think the coolest thing about confidence is that confidence is a choice,” Beck said. “With that also, I’ve said it before, it makes everyone else around you better as well. It exudes confidence into them when you’re showing that you’re confident. When you can choose that, again, you just have to go out there and execute. You have to go out there and do your thing and you have to go out there and be confident, have swag, and have moxie. Regardless of the circumstances, regardless of anything going on around you, regardless of maybe what happened the play before or maybe thinking about what’s going to happen the next play.

“You have to be in the present moment and that’s really all you can do and control.”

sports.title: Sean McVay laughs as he says he's tempted to ask assistant coach Robert Woods to suit up
sports.summary: He didn't sound completely serious, but Rams coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that he talked to assistant wide receivers coach Robert Woods about whether he could suit up and play while receivers Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all out with injuries.
sports.body:
McVay was asked during his press conference whether he has talked to the 34-year-old Woods, who was a receiver for the Rams for five years, about potentially playing again.

McVay acknowledged that there are Collective Bargaining Agreement rules against a coach becoming a player, but he said Woods is still in great shape and it would be fun to give it a try.

“I’ve looked at him, and the way he looks out there, I’ve definitely been tempted,” McVay said. “I think that’d be a violation of the CBA. I don’t know what he’d have to do, but he looks damn good and still is smooth out there. Very tempting.”

Woods was cut by the Steelers before the 2025 season and hasn’t played since, and he announced his retirement and signed a one-day contract with the Rams in February of 2026. Realistically, even with his intimate knowledge of the Rams’ offense, he probably wouldn’t be able to contribute as much on the field as whatever receiver the Rams could add off waivers or another team’s practice squad.

If Woods and the Rams actually wanted him to become an active player, it wouldn’t be as simple as signing him to the active roster, as the league has rules preventing that. Players on the reserve-retired list have to pass through waivers before they can join a team. And the NFL generally doesn’t allow coaches to become players: In 2020, when the Broncos lost all their quarterbacks to covid, they asked the league office if they could activate one of their assistant coaches and were told no. In 2009, Eagles coach Andy Reid wanted to play coaching intern Matt Nagy at quarterback in a preseason game and was also told by the league that he couldn’t.

So the idea of Woods playing receiver for the Rams is probably not going to get any kind of serious consideration. Even if, with all the Rams’ injuries, it’s tempting.

sports.title: For Week 9, Next Gen Stats outpaced the McAfee alt cast again
sports.summary: The ESPN announcement of the viewership for a given Monday night game always requires a careful look for any information about the viewership of the multiple weekly alt casts on the Disney-owned networks.
sports.body:
This week, the release presented only the total viewership for all platforms, at 21.7 million. The release also mentioned that multppe alt casts “averaged more than 900K viewers.”

Andrew Marchand of The Athletic has gotten the numbers . For the Next Gen Stats alt cast, 499,000 tuned in. For the McAfee ensemble, the number was 406,000. Making the total audience 905,000.

The final tally gives Next Gen Stats a 2-0 lead over the McAfee option. The gap was more narrow this time around; when they first squared off for the Week 6 Commanders-49ers game, NFLN attracted 469,000 and ESPN2 got 351,000 . (ESPN2 is in roughly 70 million homes; NFL Network’s distribution is at or below 50 million.)

The total viewership for that game was 17.9 million. With Bills-Vikings beating that figure by 21.2 percent, Next Gen Stats was up 6.3 percent over Week 6 and the McAfee cast increased by 15.6 percent.

Of the total audience for the game, 2.2 percent watched NFL Network and 1.87 percent watched ESPN2. Which raises, once again, a one-word question: Why?

The Monday night alt casts don’t draw in new viewers. It’s added expense, with no extra revenue for the broader operation. (Unless there’s a tangible benefit to siphoning viewers from ABC/ESPN for the other channels.)

Ultimately, it’s a zero-sum game. With alt casts, Bills-Vikings viewership was 21.7 million. Without alt casts, Bills-Vikings viewership undoubtedly would have been 21.7 million.

And that’s why the various ABC affiliates are upset that Disney will have a full slate of alt casts for Super Bowl LXI. The total number will be the total number, if the game is on one network or twenty. The alt casts will rob the Peter of ABC to pay the Paul of the various other platforms.

As the NFL is looks for more windows, and potentially heads toward more Wednesday night (and possibly Tuesday night) games, 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday continues to be the best slot.

sports.title: Broncos, Chargers announce Daiyan Henley will not be traded after all
sports.summary: More than 24 hours after the NFL trade deadline, the trade of Henley from the Charges to the Broncos was canceled.
sports.body:
Both the Chargers and the Broncos have announced that Henley will remain with the Chargers. Neither team explained why, but typically that would happen after the trade deadline only if the player failed his physical.

“The proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized,” the Broncos said in a statement. “We have great respect for Daiyan as a player and person, and we wish him all the best moving forward.”

The Chargers posted “ Welcome back, Daiyan ” on social media, about 30 hours after posting, “Thank you, Daiyan” to officially announce the trade.

According to ESPN, Henley was at the Broncos’ facility on Wednesday and took a physical, so presumably the Broncos’ medical staff decided to nix the trade. Henley did suffer a shoulder injury in Week 8 against the Rams, but he was a full participant in practice the next week and played well in Week 9 against the Texans. There have been no indications that he has had any other health concerns.

The Broncos had agreed to send a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chargers for Henley, who is in the final year of his rookie contract and is slated to become an unrestricted free agent in March.

In a memorable 2020 back-and-forth on social media , Allen and Evans engaged in a spirited debate about who was the better wide receiver.

sports.title: Dianna Russini's return includes no specifics about multiple controversies
sports.summary: As expected, Dianna Russini made her return to sports media on Wednesday, with a one-hour show platformed by an illegal offshore sports book.
sports.body:
It’s hardly a prime gig, but her “ crisis publicist ” managed to create plenty of hype — and to finagle a puff piece with People.com that included no questions about the circumstances that prompted Russini’s resignation from The Athletic .

In September, the New York Post reported that Russini would “ share her side of the scandal upon taking her next job.” She hasn’t, and she didn’t in the debut episode of her new show.

Technical difficulties delayed the release of the first episode, which was supposed to be live but seemed to be entirely pre-recorded. (The company blamed the glitch on a “record-breaking audience.” Comparable to what?)

Once the episode finally appeared, it featured three guests (none of whom are current players or coaches), preceded by a segment in which she addressed the future of Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. Which, from an editorial standpoint, is hardly the top story in the NFL on the day after the trade deadline.

There was nothing new or particularly insightful about Jackson. It was a summary of the facts that anyone who has been paying attention to the situation already knew, with a not-groundbreaking assertion that the Ravens want to keep him beyond 2026.

More significantly, the wooly mammoth in the mud room was not addressed. The overriding message was that she went away for a while, she went through some things, and now she’s back. For anyone who doesn’t know the story, she said nothing that would even begin to shed light on it.

If it’s going to be an opinions-and-interviews show, that’s fine. If she’s going to include the reporting of facts about the NFL, the credibility question can’t be ignored.

And this isn’t about the relationship (or whatever it was) with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. It’s about how she responded to it.

sports.title: Daniel Jones is "not happy" with Colts' roster purge
sports.summary: The Colts had a mini-fire sale in recent weeks, trading away four starters for future assets.
sports.body:
Quarterback Daniel Jones, not surprisingly, isn’t thrilled by the decision to send guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, receiver Keenan Allen, and receiver Josh Downs to other teams.

“I mean, honestly, you’re not you’re not happy to see it, right? ” Jones said. “You’re a player and you’re going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So you’re not happy to see a lot of those decisions, and — but like I said, it’s outside of our control, and our job is to play, be prepared, and play well. So, like I said, we got a lot of trust in the guys coming in to those spots, and we’ll be ready to go.”

It’s a bad situation for the players who remain, since it will be harder for them to win with backups thrust into the lineup. But that’s how it works whenever a non-contender admits its situation and trades players.

Those who remain have to keep going, trying to win games even if they get the impression that the front office doesn’t really care.

And even though the Jets hold the Colts’ first-round pick, a bad season for Indianapolis will result in a higher spot in every round. As the Colts embark on a rebuild, it’s not crazy to think the front office hopes to sink as low in the standings as possible, since that will enhance the priority of the picks they have.

The Jets will welcome that, since they have the Colts’ first-round pick. Thanks to the failed trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner.

Brady pointed to Hooker’s status as a “savvy” and “cerebral” eight-year NFL veteran who oozes “football intelligence” with a ton of experience to boot. Fortunately, he was on a bye this past week with his old team, the Tennessee Titans. However, arriving on Wednesday and having to navigate everything that comes with packing up and moving to a new city is no small feat for an NFL player. For his part, Hooker sounds ready to go, and very excited, admitting that he’s “on social media, so I hear all the rumors,” which means he probably had a feeling something was brewing. When asked about the challenge of changing teams midseason, Hooker didn’t hesitate in stepping up to the plate, saying “I pride myself on being a pro and being ready when my name is called no matter what.” His plan? Hooker will soak up all he can with his coaches this week, putting in “a little overtime this week and get up to speed on the style of play we want here, and just deliver.” When asked just how different is Leonhard’s scheme is, Hooker simply said that “at the end of the day, it’s football. Every team runs Cover 4. Every team runs Cover 2, and Cover 3. So, it’s really just about terminology, and what they call different things , and how they play certain looks. sports.title: Kirk Cousins plans to talk to Jakobe Thomas about No. 8
sports.summary: Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins made his official return to the team on Wednesday.
sports.body:
Has he spoken to rookie safety Jakobe Thomas, who currently wears No. 8?

“I need to circle back with him,” Cousins told reporters. “Haven’t gotten there. So we’ll have a conversation and I think Mike Parsons will help us, too, in the equipment room. But, yeah, I’ve got to talk to Jakobe for sure.”

When the issue came up again later, Cousins laughed — while also making his intentions clear: “I’m confident that Jakobe and I can have a healthy and mature conversation and figure this out.”

sports.title: Kevin O'Connell on Kyler Murray: I want him to get healthy, you never know what could happen
sports.summary: The Vikings made Kyler Murray their quarterback choice to open the 2026 season, but it didn't take long for their plans to go awry.
sports.body:
Murray was concussed early in the season opener, missed Week 2 and then led an underwhelming offense to a 4-1 record before suffering a hamstring injury in Week 8. The Vikings offense got even worse with Carson Wentz in Monday night’s loss to the Bills, which led the team to trade for Kirk Cousins on Tuesday.

Head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn’t committed to starting Cousins against the Packers this weekend, but it’s why the deal was made and Murray isn’t currently an option because he remained out of practice with a hamstring injury on Wednesday. Once Murray is healthy, he’ll be slated for a backup role as O’Connell said he doesn’t believe “you can have a competition during the season” and that his hope is that Murray is available if and when the Vikings have to pivot again.

“The reality is what it is ,” O’Connell said. “It’s one of those things where I think he appreciated hearing about it before the transaction took place, but at the same time, he knows I believe in him. I believe in Kyler, just like I believe in Carson and I believe in Max [Brosmer]. I want him to get healthy and get back to work because you just never know. We do not hold the cards in how this will go from a health standpoint or anything like that with anybody on our team.”

O’Connell said that he told Murray that he knows it has been a “less than ideal” series of events, but that underscores the possibility that the Vikings will have to turn back to him with an important game on the line at some point later this year.

sports.title: Zac Taylor: Duke Tobin is "really apologetic" after backing out of trade with Eagles
sports.summary: On Tuesday, the Bengals backed out of a trade for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie after it was revealed that the deal might cost Cincinnati with a future compensatory draft pick.
sports.body:
During his Wednesday press conference, head coach Zac Taylor explained the situation from the perspective of Bengals director of player personnel — and de facto General Manager — Duke Tobin.

“Obviously, we tried something yesterday ,” Taylor said. “Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me about how he wanted this portrayed. I’m not comfortable doing it, but I’m going to do what he asked. We did make an effort to put some depth in there in place of Cashius [Howell]. As we got into it, it was going to be more costly than we initially anticipated.

“He’s really apologetic about it and wants it made clear — Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our end. Certainly, we have a ton of confidence in our front office and how they do things. They’ve given us the players that have allowed us to be 6-2 right now, and playing at such a high level. So, we’ll put that behind us and move forward, and just get excited for this game on Sunday. Our locker room is in a great place right now.”

Taylor noted Tobin didn’t really tell him how everything went down and he didn’t ask the question.

“It doesn’t really matter to me. It probably took three minutes of my day yesterday away from watching tape,” Taylor said. “So, got a lot of faith in how those guys operate and we’ll just move forward with it.”

With that, the Bengals didn’t make any deadline moves to improve the team. Taylor said he and Tobin like where the team is.

“I think you can talk to the players in the locker room, they really like where we’re at,” Taylor said. “So, this is a team with a lot of confidence right now. I know it’s a fun period of time — the weeks leading up to the trade deadline — for fans … but the truth is, we really like where we’re at. Our guys are playing with a high degree of confidence and we’ll continue to move forward.”
