sports.body: The Jets recently signed former Steelers defensive lineman Isaiahh Loudermilk to their practice squad. Today, we break him down in detail. The 29-year old Loudermilk is listed at 6’7” and 293 pounds and was a fifth round pick out of Wisconsin in 2021. He has started seven games in his NFL career, with 63 tackles, six passes defensed and one sack. Background Loudermilk was a three-star high school recruit despite only having played 8-man football in a small town. He ended up going to Wisconsin, where he redshirted his first season in 2016, but then became a useful player over the next few years. In 2017, Loudermilk had six tackles in 11 games in a reserve role, adding 1.5 sacks and a pass defensed. He started the first six games of his career in 2018 and ended up with 15 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, three passes defensed and a sack in nine games. In 2019, he started all 14 games and had his most productive season with 24 tackles, five tackles for loss, three sacks, five pass breakups and two forced fumbles. However, Loudermilk got all Big-10 recognition for the only time in his final season as he was named as a third-teamer by the media and an honorable mention by the coaches. In just six games during the pandemic-shortened 2020 season, he had 13 tackles and two sacks. After not being invited to the scouting combine, Loudermilk played in the East-West Shrine Bowl and was eventually drafted by the Steelers in the fifth round of the 2021 draft. As a rookie, he started two games and ended up with 23 tackles, a sack and two pass breakups in 15 appearances. In 2022, Loudermilk started three times but had just seven tackles and a tackle for loss in 11 games overall. He played in 16 games in both 2023 and 2024 but did not start a game during that time. He ended up with 33 tackles, three passes defensed and a quarterback hit over the two seasons. 2025 saw Loudermilk start the first two games, although he didn’t generate any statistics. An injury in the second game sidelined him for the rest of the season. He was almost ready to return for the postseason but wasn’t cleared in time. Loudermilk signed for the Vikings in the offseason but failed to make their roster and was eventually added to the Jets’ practice squad last month. sports.title: Todd Monken: I intend for Deshaun Watson being our starting QB
sports.summary: Monken said he doesn't anticipate making a quarterback change while confirming Watson's Week 10 return.
sports.body:
Watson did not play last week after missing a pair of practices while in the concussion protocol and the team’s plans for this Sunday remained a topic of conversation because Monken declined to say who would start during a Monday press conference. Monken explained that response by saying that he wanted to talk to the team’s coaching staff before adding that he also didn’t feel a need to make a public proclamation.

“Ultimately, the full body of work , the previous eight games we had played,” Monken said. “Deshaun played pretty well. That was my intention, I just wanted to make sure to run it by my staff before I said it publicly. I don’t know why I have to say it publicly.”

Monken was asked if he will be making a quarterback determination on a weekly basis moving forward.

“I don’t look at it week-to-week and I don’t look at it as long term,” Monken said. “We’re judged each week. I am, he is, our team is. . . . I anticipate him being our starter. That’s what he’s been, he’s been our starter. . . . I have no intention of Deshaun not being our starter.”

The Texans are 5-4 heading into their game with the Texans and they have a bye in Week 11. If they are unable to stay on the right side of .500 after that break, Monken will likely field more questions about the plan for Watson moving forward.

Instead, they leaned on James Cook, a defense that refused to let the Minnesota Vikings find the end zone, and a young tight end who delivered one of the biggest moments of his career. Buffalo’s 23-6 victory over Minnesota was a team effort, and head coach Joe Brady’s postgame Game Balls reflected exactly that. His five-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter capped a 15-play, 84-yard drive that drained 8:32 off the clock and effectively put the game out of reach. Brady also recognized Cook for reaching the 5,000-career-rushing-yard milestone, another significant accomplishment for Buffalo’s running back. The milestone adds to a night when Cook carried the offense, helping the Bills dominate time of possession and secure their second consecutive victory. Cook continues to prove he can be more than an explosive-play threat. When the Bills need to grind out yards, extend possessions, and keep their defense fresh, he’s more than capable of carrying the workload. Instead, they controlled the clock, leaned heavily on James Cook, and delivered one of their most complete defensive performances of the season in a 23-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings. Buffalo held the ball for an incredible 42:32, leaving Minnesota’s offense on the field for just 17:28. The Bills ran 80 offensive snaps compared to only 48 defensive snaps, a significant workload difference that tells much of the story. Minnesota finished with just 178 total yards, nine first downs, an 0-for-8 performance on third down, and failed on both fourth-down attempts. The Vikings also committed three turnovers. Offense: 80 snaps James Cook played 51 offensive snaps (64%), finishing with 31 carries for 107 yards and a touchdown. That’s a substantial workload, particularly considering Buffalo ran the ball 44 times. Cook averaged just 3.5 yards per carry, but his production wasn’t about explosive plays. It was about keeping the offense moving, wearing down Minnesota’s defense, and helping Buffalo control the clock. Ty Johnson played 17 snaps (21%), while Ray Davis saw 11 (14%). Johnson contributed a 36-yard reception on third-and-eight, Buffalo’s longest offensive play of the night. The distribution is interesting because Cook accounted for 31 of Buffalo’s 44 rushing attempts despite playing just 64% of the offensive snaps. When Cook was on the field, the Bills clearly wanted the ball in his hands. sports.title: Report: Giants called Falcons about a potential Bijan Robinson trade
sports.summary: The Giants didn't make any big deals at the trade deadline, but they tried to make a very big one.
sports.body:
The Giants called the Falcons to see whether running back Bijan Robinson was available in a trade, according to Jordan Raanan of ESPN.

That would have been a blockbuster, but it’s unsurprising that the teams didn’t make a deal. The Falcons made a big investment in Robinson this offseason, signing him to a three-year, $66.8 million contract extension, and from all accounts they view him as one of the most important pieces of their franchise.

There’s no word on what the Giants were willing to offer, or whether the Falcons engaged at all, or simply told the Giants, “Not interested.”

The Giants did make one big trade this season, acquiring J.J. McCarthy, who has played well enough for the Giants to win their first two starts and remain in first place in the NFC East. Acquiring Robinson would have been a strong sign that the Giants believe they’re serious contenders, this year. That the Giants even tried showed that coach John Harbaugh meant it when he said they’re a team trying to win now , not build for the future.

sports.body: A year after making a pair of franchise-altering deals at the NFL trade deadline, the Jets stayed quiet this year. The only trade they made was a minor one, sending backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions in exchange for a future sixth round pick. The Jets did not trade defensive end Will McDonald despite McDonald requesting a deal to a new team and other teams reportedly having interest. [Media: https://twitter.com/Schultz_Report/status/2119841495251624248] It probably shouldn’t be a massive surprise to see the Jets stay out of the trade market. At 2-7, there would be no way to justify this team being a buyer. At the same time, a coaching staff and possibly front office fighting for its respective jobs might not be willing to give up quality players in exchange for future Draft picks they might not be around to make. So we ended up with a trade deadline that lacked much activity for this team.
